scenarios.name: Imposed-B Native Curvature Test
scenarios.description: Controlled response of a mobile polarity to the selected native velocity-cross-curl force in an imposed Bz=1 field.

comment.physical_purpose: Measures magnetic curvature against an otherwise identical no-Lorentz control.
comment.parameters: Bz=1 imposed through J=(-B*y/2,B*x/2,0); one positive polarity at v=(0.12,0,0). The stated alpha*B*dt<0.01 bound holds in the INTERIOR ONLY: a single-valued linear vector potential cannot carry a uniform B on a periodic lattice, so compensating return flux appears at the seam. Recomputing the engine curl with periodic neighbours gives interior Bz=+1.0 but face slabs Bz=1-N/4 and corner columns 1-N/2 (per-plane sum exactly 0). At the shipped browser default L=33 that is -7.25 / -15.50 over ~11.8% of the volume, i.e. wrong-signed and up to 15.5x oversized, with alpha*max|B|*dt ~ 0.113 there. The certifying test probes a single interior site.
comment.expected_behavior: The Lorentz-enabled branch curves toward -y while the matched no-Lorentz control remains straight.
comment.discrepancy: The vector potential and force law are selected inputs. The result does not establish EM emergence, a physical charge calibration, or a continuum cyclotron orbit. The imposed field is NOT uniform over the whole lattice (see parameters): the B-field overlay displays a wrong-signed sheet on the boundary slabs. The sibling s0-field-uniform-b already books this finite-face limitation explicitly; this card did not until 2026-07-26.
